    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Cavern C2 Uses DNS and Google Apps Script to Blend Into Legitimate Traffic
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

ATT&CKT1190

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] GHSA-m5w8-4gq2-6f8x: vm2: NodeVM `builtin: ['*']` exposes `os`
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Node.js process direct DNS egress to external resolver (vm2 dns.setServers host hijack)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Node.js process direct DNS egress to external resolver (vm2 dns.setServers host hijack) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the observable side-effect of the vm2 NodeVM `builtin:['*']` sandbox escape: sandbox code calls `dns.setServers(['attacker.example:53'])` then `dns.resolve()`, causing the host node process to send DNS queries straight to an attacker-controlled resolver on port 53. A node runtime talking UDP/TCP 53 directly to a public, non-sanctioned resolver IP is anomalous because normal Node code uses `dns.lookup`/getaddrinfo through the OS stub resolver, not c-ares direct-to-resolver egress. Rationale: Uses the article's strongest primitive [E] — `dns.setServers()` + `dns.resolve()` — whose only host-visible artifact is the node process itself sending DNS to a new resolver IP on port 53 (c-ares direct egress, unlike the normal getaddrinfo/dns.lookup path). Pivots on node binary + RemotePort 53 + public/non-sanctioned resolver, which is high-fidelity because legit Node rarely talks raw 53 to an arbitrary external IP. Detection is behavioral (no IOCs exist in this vuln advisory), so no external IOC corroboration was applicable.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1557
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Node service that legitimately runs its own DNS-over-HTTPS/DoT bootstrap or a custom c-ares resolver pointed at a fixed public resolver (8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1 already excluded)
  • Node-based network monitoring or service-discovery agent (e.g. consul/etcd clients, uptime probes) issuing dns.resolve() to an external resolver by design
  • Developer workstations running Node tooling configured with NODE_OPTIONS / custom resolver against a cloud DNS provider
  • Container sidecar or CoreDNS-adjacent Node app performing SRV/TXT lookups directly against an upstream forwarder
  • App that resolves via a corporate secondary resolver hosted in a cloud VPC that presents as a public IP
Suppression filter
| where RemoteIP !in ("8.8.8.8","8.8.4.4","1.1.1.1","1.0.0.1","9.9.9.9","149.112.112.112") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dns-result-order","doh","dns-over-https") )
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full RemoteIP set and command line for the node process — is the destination a known corporate/cloud resolver, and does this host normally run vm2-based code (multi-tenant sandbox, template engine, serverless eval)? Whois/threat-intel the resolver IP. 2) Contain: if the resolver is unrecognized, isolate the host/container and block egress to that IP:53; treat any credentials, tokens, or npm installs performed after the first-seen timestamp as potentially redirected. 3) Hunt: on the same host look for subsequent connections to unexpected IPs for registry.npmjs.org / OIDC issuer hostnames (setServers → poisoned resolution), review the app for `builtin:['*']` NodeVM config, and pivot org-wide for other node hosts hitting the same resolver IP.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where RemotePort == 53
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemoteIP !in ("8.8.8.8","8.8.4.4","1.1.1.1","1.0.0.1","9.9.9.9","149.112.112.112")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), ConnCount=count() by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
ASCDeviceEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where RemotePort == 53
| where isnotempty(RemoteIP)
| where not(ipv4_is_private(RemoteIP))

Node.js runtime spawning a shell/command interpreter (vm2 sandbox breakout RCE) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the host-observable manifestation of a vm2 sandbox escape (CVE-2026-47698): the Node.js process breaking out of the JS sandbox and invoking child_process to run OS commands, surfacing as node/node.exe as the parent of sh/bash/cmd/powershell. Article-specific because the PoC's payload path is `e.constructor.constructor("return process")().mainModule.require('child_process').execSync(...)`, which always terminates in a shell child of the Node host. Rationale: Uses the invariant tail of the article's PoC — the sandbox escape always lands in child_process.execSync/exec, forcing node to become the parent of a shell. Parent=node + child=interpreter is the highest-fidelity host pivot for this bug class; cross-checked against the GitLab advisory and patriksimek/vm2 GHSA history confirming the child_process RCE sink. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-47698/ • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-grj5-jjm8-h35p
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Node build tooling (webpack, npm/yarn lifecycle scripts, node-gyp) invoking sh/cmd to run install or build steps
  • CI/CD runner hosts where a Node orchestrator legitimately shells out per pipeline step
  • Node apps wrapping native binaries via child_process (ffmpeg/imagemagick, git, pdftk)
  • Process managers such as pm2 spawning shell wrappers for managed apps
  • Electron desktop apps spawning helper shells
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm","npm-cli.js","node-gyp","yarn","webpack","react-scripts","pm2") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("webpack","react-scripts","jest","node-gyp"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the child ProcessCommandLine and the parent Node app path/cmdline. Legit build/CI shell-outs run bounded commands (npm, git, node-gyp); reconnaissance/whoami/curl/base64/wget or writes to web-root or /tmp are hostile. Check if the host runs an internet-facing service that evaluates user-supplied JS via vm2. 2) Contain: isolate the host and suspend/kill the offending node process tree; snapshot for IR. 3) Hunt: on the same host look for a subsequently written marker/payload file (the PoC drops 'pwned'), new outbound connections from node, added persistence, and confirm the vm2 package version (<=3.11.5) present in the app's node_modules.
DeviceProcessEvents

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.5) exposed to CVE-2026-47698 sandbox breakout AIExploitation High
Surfaces hosts/apps carrying the vm2 npm package at a version vulnerable to the dangerous-host-proto-mutator sandbox breakout (CVE-2026-47698, fixed in 3.11.6). This is the exploitable-surface pivot: any service that evaluates untrusted JavaScript through a pre-3.11.6 vm2 is one crafted input away from host RCE. Rationale: Concrete versioned exposure from the advisory: affected npm:vm2 <=3.11.5, fixed 3.11.6, tracked as CVE-2026-47698 (confirmed via GitLab advisory). Filtering on the CVE id or the vm2 package name in TVM inventory gives a low-FP exposure list to prioritize patching before the process-behavior UC ever needs to fire. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-47698/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cfcw-xp6x-25gj
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A vm2 install already at 3.11.6+ still tagged by a stale scanner cache (verify SoftwareVersion)
  • Bundled/vendored vm2 copies inside a larger app where the version string is not cleanly parsed
  • Developer workstations with vm2 in dev-only dependencies not reachable by untrusted input
  • Test fixtures or security-research copies of vm2 intentionally kept at a vulnerable version
  • Container image layers reported per-host inflating device counts for the same artifact
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVersion !in ("3.11.6") and not (SoftwareVersion startswith "3.12" or SoftwareVersion startswith "4.")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the reported SoftwareVersion is genuinely <=3.11.5 and identify whether the host runs a service that feeds attacker-controllable JavaScript into vm2 (code-eval, plugin engines, template sandboxes). 2) Contain: prioritize the patch to vm2>=3.11.6 (or remove vm2 in favor of isolated-vm) on internet-facing/eval-exposed services first; add WAF/input controls where patching lags. 3) Hunt: pivot the affected DeviceNames into the Node-spawns-shell detection to check whether exploitation has already occurred, and review app logs for anomalous eval inputs.

Node.js runtime spawning shell/recon child process (vm2 CVE-2026-47686 escape RCE) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the host-observable manifestation of a vm2 Error.cause sandbox escape: a Node.js parent process spawning a command interpreter or reconnaissance utility via child_process (the PoC runs execSync('id')). Node backend services rarely legitimately spawn shells, making parent=node + child=shell/id/whoami a high-value escape signal. Rationale: Anchors on the PoC's exact escape payload (node -> child_process -> execSync('id')) using parent=node + child=shell/id/whoami; corroborated by Kodem and SentinelOne write-ups that name Node.js parents spawning shells/interpreters as the primary runtime signal for the 2026 vm2 CVE wave. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-47686/ • https://www.kodemsecurity.com/resources/vm2-sandbox-escape-vulnerabilities-the-2026-cve-wave-turning-ai-agents-into-host-rce-vectors • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-26956/
ATT&CKT1059 T1059.004 T1211
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Node build tooling / npm lifecycle scripts (node spawning sh -c to run gulp, webpack, node-gyp)
  • Legitimate apps that shell out to media/PDF tools (ffmpeg, imagemagick, ghostscript wrappers)
  • CI/CD runners executing node scripts that call git/curl via child_process
  • Health-check or monitoring node services running whoami/id/uname for diagnostics
  • Serverless/container entrypoints where node PID 1 spawns sh as the init shim
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("webpack","node-gyp","gulp","ffmpeg","imagemagick","ghostscript","npm run","git ") )
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the child ProcessCommandLine and the node parent's command line; confirm whether the node service is an internet-facing app that ingests untrusted input via vm2. Benign build/media wrappers use predictable args (webpack, ffmpeg) — escape payloads run ad-hoc recon (id, whoami, uname) or download tools. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the node process tree, and snapshot for forensics; block any outbound IP the child contacted. 3) Hunt: enumerate installed vm2 versions on the fleet (see companion UC), review the app's request logs for the input that triggered the throw-with-cause, and search for follow-on persistence, credential access, or C2 from the same node PID.

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","id","whoami","uname","curl.exe","curl","wget","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildProcess = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","/sh","/bash","/dash","/zsh","id","whoami","uname","curl","wget","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable vm2 package present on host (CVE-2026-47686, vm2 <= 3.11.5) AIReconnaissance High
Surfaces hosts running a vm2 version vulnerable to the Error.cause sandbox-escape-to-RCE (fixed in 3.11.6) so the attack surface can be patched before exploitation. Keyed on the concrete CVE id and the vm2 package name from the advisory. Rationale: Uses the exact advisory identifiers — CveId CVE-2026-47686 and the vm2 package name — against endpoint vulnerability inventory; fixed version 3.11.6 confirmed via GitLab advisory so any lower version on inventory is a true positive attack surface. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-47686/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m283-3h24-438v
ATT&CKT1211 T1059
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • vm2 pinned but embedder never throws Error with .cause referencing a host object (not exploitable, but still worth patching)
  • Transitive vm2 dependency inside a dev-only/test package that never runs untrusted input
  • Scanner reporting the package inside a node_modules cache that is not actually deployed/executed
  • Already-remediated hosts where inventory lags the 3.11.6 upgrade by a scan cycle
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the reported vm2 version is <= 3.11.5 and whether the hosting service exposes a host function that throws new Error(msg, {cause: <hostObj>}); that prerequisite is what makes it exploitable. 2) Contain: prioritize patch to vm2 3.11.6+ (including transitive deps) and, as interim mitigation, audit embedder code for error-chaining that leaks host references into sandboxed catch blocks. 3) Hunt: on any host that cannot be immediately patched, deploy the companion runtime detection for node spawning shells/recon utilities and review app request logs for inputs that force the host function to throw.

New API CVE-2026-71479: integer-overflow multiplier in billing request (self-crediting) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound requests to New API generation endpoints carrying an oversized user-controlled multiplier (`n`, duration) that wraps quota math negative — e.g. the in-the-wild value n=18446744073686646784. Article-specific because it keys on the exact near-uint64 overflow value and the multiplier parameter abused for self-crediting. Rationale: Keys on the exact ITW overflow value 18446744073686646784 and the abused `n`/duration multiplier on New API image/audio endpoints — both cross-checked against the GitLab advisory and securityonline write-up. Any n far above the realistic 1-10 image count, or a ~1.8e19 integer, is a wrapped-negative overflow attempt. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/quantumnous/new-api/CVE-2026-71479/ • https://securityonline.info/cve-2026-71479-new-api-integer-overflow/ • https://github.com/QuantumNous/new-api/releases/tag/v1.0.0-rc.18
ATT&CKT1190 T1657
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Operator load/stress testing the API with deliberately large batch sizes
  • Legitimate gallery generation requesting n=10 (below the >1000 threshold, filtered)
  • Request-ID, trace-ID or nanosecond timestamp fields that happen to be 19-digit integers matching the near-uint64 regex
  • Token-count / max_tokens fields carrying large-but-legitimate values
Suppression filter
| where not (SyslogMessage has_any ("request_id","trace_id","traceId","X-Request-Id")) or SyslogMessage has "18446744073686646784"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request line and the authenticated user/token that sent it; confirm the multiplier (`n`/duration) is far outside legitimate range and whether the value equals/near 2^64. 2) Contain: suspend the offending account/API token and freeze its wallet balance; if the instance is <= v1.0.0-rc.17, upgrade to v1.0.0-rc.18+ immediately (the overflow is unauthenticated-equivalent when free-seed features are on). 3) Hunt: pivot on the account's consume/task log for negative settlement entries (UC2), review all balances for abnormal inflation, and check for mass-registration from the same source IP feeding free seed balance.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("new-api","/v1/images/generations","/v1/audio/speech","quota")
| where SyslogMessage has "18446744073686646784"
   or SyslogMessage matches regex @'"n"\s*:\s*\d{4,}'
   or SyslogMessage matches regex @'\b1[0-9]{18,19}\b'   // integers near the uint64 ceiling (~1.8e19) = wrapped-negative overflow
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, HostIP, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New API CVE-2026-71479: negative quota settlement / quota_saturation self-crediting AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the impact signature of the overflow — negative consumption/charge entries at settlement and the vendor-added `admin_info.quota_saturation` audit flag (rc.19+) — that indicate a wallet was credited instead of debited. This is the confirmation/impact pivot distinct from the inbound request. Rationale: Uses the two impact artifacts named in the advisory: the purpose-built `quota_saturation` audit flag added in v1.0.0-rc.19 and the 'large negative consumption entries in logs' the community reporter observed. A negative settlement is definitionally a credit and is the highest-fidelity confirmation of exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8r8v-xf7q-rcpr • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/quantumnous/new-api/CVE-2026-71479/ • https://github.com/QuantumNous/new-api/issues/5235
ATT&CKT1657
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate pre-consume refunds on streaming-response client disconnect (New API issue #5235) recorded as negative consume
  • Admin manual balance top-ups/adjustments logged as negative charge entries
  • Benign quota_saturation clamps on a patched (rc.18/rc.19) instance where the saturating conversion fired on an honest large-but-valid request
  • Failed-request rollback of pre-consumed quota (normal negative refund)
Suppression filter
| where not (SyslogMessage has_any ("client disconnect","stream closed","refund","admin adjust","manual top-up")) or SyslogMessage has "quota_saturation"
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each hit, identify the user/token and the request that produced the negative settlement; compare the negative magnitude to the account's normal spend and check whether balance jumped immediately after. 2) Contain: freeze the account balance and revoke its tokens; snapshot the consume/task log rows for evidence; verify the instance is patched to v1.0.0-rc.18+ and audit `admin_info.quota_saturation` across all users. 3) Hunt: enumerate every account whose balance rose without a corresponding top-up, correlate back to the crafted overflow requests (UC1), and review upstream prepaid provider spend for drain.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has "quota_saturation"
   or SyslogMessage matches regex @'(?i)(quota|consume|charge)["''\s:=]{1,4}-\d{3,}'   // negative multi-digit settlement = credit
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, HostIP, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

new-api CVE-2026-64859: admin user-list/detail API access token disclosure scoping AIExploitation Medium
Hunts authenticated access to the new-api admin user-management endpoints (GET /api/user/, /api/user/search, /api/user/<id>) that serialize the access_token field and can leak the root user's bearer token. Because access logs don't expose the JSON body, this scopes which admin source IPs could have harvested tokens so responders know whose credentials to rotate, and flags enumeration-style scraping of many user records. Rationale: Uses the exact guarded routes confirmed from new-api's router/api-router.go (adminRoute GET '/', '/search', '/:id' -> /api/user/*) which the advisory names as the leak vector; GET+200 on /api/user/* is the only signal available from access logs since the token lives in the response body. Cross-checked GHSA-6x2c-phff-wx57 and the GitLab advisory mirror. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x2c-phff-wx57 • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/quantumnous/new-api/CVE-2026-64859/ • https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QuantumNous/new-api/main/router/api-router.go
ATT&CKT1528 T1087
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Root/admin operator legitimately browsing the user list in the console (GET /api/user/)
  • Automated user-provisioning, SCIM sync, or billing export scripts iterating user records
  • Monitoring/health probes hitting /api/user/self
  • Support staff opening individual user detail pages (/api/user/<id>)
  • Load-balancer or uptime checks against the /api path
Suppression filter
| where DistinctPaths >= 5 OR Requests >= 20   // require enumeration/scraping of many user records rather than a single admin viewing one user
Response runbook
1) Triage: For each cIP/csUsername surfaced, confirm whether the account is a NON-root admin (the CVE threat is admin->root escalation). Note the time window and whether DistinctPaths indicates single-record view vs. bulk enumeration. 2) Contain: Immediately rotate the root access token and any other user access tokens (Personal Settings > System Access Token), then upgrade new-api to v1.0.0-rc.7+ which changes the field to json:"-". Invalidate active sessions for the flagged admin. 3) Hunt: Pivot each suspect cIP into UC2 to see if it subsequently hit root-only /api/option/ endpoints; review /api/option/ config changes (SMTP/OAuth/payment) around that time for tampering.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "GET"
| where csUriStem startswith "/api/user/"   // GetAllUsers '/', SearchUsers '/search', GetUser '/:id' -- all serialize access_token
| where scStatus == 200
| summarize Requests=count(), DistinctPaths=dcount(csUriStem), Paths=make_set(csUriStem, 50), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by cIP, csUsername, sSiteName
| order by Requests desc

new-api CVE-2026-64859: root-only /api/option config change following user-record access from same IP AIActions on Objectives Medium
Correlates a source IP accessing the token-leaking admin user endpoints (GET /api/user/*) with that same IP subsequently invoking root-only system-config endpoints (PUT /api/option/, POST /api/option/payment_compliance, POST /api/option/rest_model_ratio) within 30 minutes. This captures the privilege-escalation chain: an admin harvests the root access token then reuses it as a bearer credential to modify SMTP/OAuth/payment and other root-only settings. Rationale: Encodes the actual escalation described in the advisory: /api/option/ endpoints are guarded by RootAuth() in api-router.go, so a client IP that scraped /api/user/* (RootAuth-leaking data) and then drives a root-only config write is the concrete steal-token-then-reuse signature. Endpoints and their auth middleware were verified from new-api source; advisory confirmed via GHSA-6x2c-phff-wx57. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x2c-phff-wx57 • https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QuantumNous/new-api/main/router/api-router.go
ATT&CKT1078 T1528
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • The legitimate root user (who is also an admin) browsing users then changing a system setting in the same console session from one IP
  • Multiple staff behind a shared NAT/proxy egress IP where a root operator's config change collapses onto an admin's user-list view
  • Infrastructure-as-code / automation that both provisions users and pushes option config from a single management host
  • A pentest or configuration-audit run touching both endpoints
  • Reverse-proxy that rewrites all client IPs to a single upstream address (breaks per-user attribution)
Suppression filter
// In the userEnum let-block, require enumeration rather than a single incidental view before correlating:
// | summarize EnumTime=min(TimeGenerated), EnumPaths=dcount(csUriStem) by cIP | where EnumPaths >= 3
Response runbook
1) Triage: Confirm the cIP does NOT belong to the sanctioned root operator/jump host, and identify which /api/option/ setting changed (payment, SMTP, OAuth) by pulling the request around OptTime; a non-root admin IP writing root config is the true positive. 2) Contain: Rotate the root access token and all admin tokens, revert any unauthorized /api/option/ changes (especially OAuth/SMTP/payment), block the source IP, and upgrade to new-api v1.0.0-rc.7+. 3) Hunt: Sweep all /api/option/ writes and /api/user/* reads from the same IP over the prior 30 days, review outbound mail/OAuth callback config for attacker-controlled endpoints, and check for new admin/user accounts or token creations made with the stolen root context.
let win = 30m;
let userEnum = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csMethod == "GET" and scStatus == 200
    | where csUriStem startswith "/api/user/"
    | project EnumTime=TimeGenerated, cIP, EnumPath=csUriStem;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where scStatus == 200
| where (csMethod == "PUT" and csUriStem =~ "/api/option/")
     or (csMethod == "POST" and csUriStem in~ ("/api/option/payment_compliance","/api/option/rest_model_ratio"))
| project OptTime=TimeGenerated, cIP, OptMethod=csMethod, OptPath=csUriStem, csUsername, sSiteName
| join kind=inner userEnum on cIP
| where OptTime between (EnumTime .. EnumTime + win)
| project EnumTime, OptTime, DelayMin=datetime_diff('minute', OptTime, EnumTime), cIP, EnumPath, OptMethod, OptPath, sSiteName
| order by OptTime desc

conflibot command injection: shell spawned by Node action with git + shell metacharacters (CVE-2026-55158) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner where the conflibot Node action spawns a shell that runs a git command whose arguments contain shell metacharacters ($( ), backtick, ;, |, &). Under pull_request_target these metacharacters come from an attacker-controlled PR head.ref, so their presence in a conflibot-invoked git shell is the direct signature of CVE-2026-55158 command injection. Rationale: Anchors on the exact vulnerable mechanism the advisory describes: conflibot (a Node action) building git commands by string interpolation and running them through a shell, with head.ref branch names carrying shell metacharacters `$( ) ; | & backtick. Parent=node + child shell + literal 'git' + a metacharacter regex is a tight, article-specific signature rather than a generic shell-injection template. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2qvg-qr73-mqxp • https://github.com/wktk/conflibot • https://research.jfrog.com/post/part-1-pull-request-target-exploitation/ • https://orca.security/resources/blog/pull-request-nightmare-github-actions-rce/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1195.001 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate PR branch name that happens to contain a pipe or semicolon passed to a benign git log/diff step
  • Custom in-house CI tooling built on Node that shells out to git with pipelines (e.g. `git log | grep`)
  • Developers running git one-liners with command substitution inside a Node-based dev container on the same host
  • Monorepo automation that chains git commands with `&&` inside a shell invoked by a Node CLI
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("git log","git diff","git grep") and ProcessCommandLine !matches regex @"refs/(heads|pull)/")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the offending ProcessCommandLine and the parent InitiatingProcessCommandLine; extract the branch/ref string and confirm it contains attacker-supplied metacharacters. Identify the repo and PR number from the runner's /_work path and check whether the PR came from an external fork. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the self-hosted runner, revoke/rotate the repo GITHUB_TOKEN and any secrets exposed to the pull_request_target job, and disable the conflibot workflow until upgraded to wktk/conflibot@v2 (>=1.2.1). 3) HUNT: On the same runner, look for child processes of the injected shell (curl/wget/nc/base64/openssl), outbound connections to unknown hosts, reads of env/token files, and any `git push` from the runner in the minutes after the event.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","nodejs")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "git"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"[`;&|]|\$\("
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("conflibot","/_actions/","actions/runner","Runner.Worker","/_work/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","nodejs")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "git"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"[`;&|]|\$\("
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("conflibot","/_actions/","actions/runner","Runner.Worker","/_work/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine

conflibot post-injection secret exfiltration: token grab by git/shell child on CI runner (CVE-2026-55158) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the second stage of CVE-2026-55158: after command injection on the runner, the injected git/shell process spawns a network or encoding tool (curl, wget, nc, base64, openssl) whose command line references the runner's GITHUB_TOKEN / ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN. This is how an attacker exfiltrates the write-scoped token and base-repo secrets the pull_request_target job exposes. Rationale: Targets the advisory's stated impact — exfiltrate secrets and the write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN — with a distinct pivot from UC1 (network/encoding tool child + explicit token env-var strings rather than the injection metacharacters). The GITHUB_TOKEN / ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN references parented by git/shell/node on a runner are high-fidelity because benign conflibot only runs git. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2qvg-qr73-mqxp • https://research.jfrog.com/post/part-1-pull-request-target-exploitation/ • https://orca.security/resources/blog/pull-request-nightmare-github-actions-rce/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1041 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate CI step that curls an internal artifact repo using an auth header sourced from GITHUB_TOKEN
  • Actions cache/toolkit uploads that reference ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN in a child curl
  • Base64-encoding of build artifacts inside a git/node-driven pipeline step
  • openssl invoked for legitimate TLS/cert operations by CI tooling with token env inherited but not exfiltrated
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName =~ "curl" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("api.github.com","ghcr.io","pkg.actions.githubusercontent.com","results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Capture the child command line and its destination (RemoteUrl/RemoteIP from DeviceNetworkEvents for the same process); confirm whether the token value is being sent to an external, non-GitHub host. Tie back to the PR/fork that triggered the conflibot job. 2) CONTAIN: Immediately revoke and rotate the exposed GITHUB_TOKEN, the repo/org secrets available to the workflow, and any downstream credentials; isolate the runner and review repo audit log for pushes or workflow changes made with the token. 3) HUNT: Search the org for other pull_request_target workflows invoking vulnerable conflibot (<1.2.1), review git push events and new tags/releases from runner IPs, and check for new outbound C2 destinations from CI infrastructure.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git","sh","bash","dash","node")
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","nc","ncat","base64","openssl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("GITHUB_TOKEN","ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN","RUNNER_TOKEN","/proc/self/environ","printenv","refs/pull")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("git","sh","bash","dash","node")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","nc","ncat","base64","openssl")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("GITHUB_TOKEN","ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN","RUNNER_TOKEN","/proc/self/environ","printenv","refs/pull")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Clop hex-named JSP webshell dropped under PTC Windchill /login (CVE-2026-12569) AIInstallation High
Hunts creation of 16-hex-character or dpr_<8hex> named .jsp files written under the Windchill/login application directory, plus the known campaign SHA256. This is the webshell Clop drops after exploiting the FlexPLM WSDL + Windchill login-servlet RCE chain, and the filename convention is article/campaign-specific. Rationale: Uses the campaign-specific webshell filename regex [0-9a-f]{16}.jsp / dpr_<8hex>.jsp under /Windchill/login/ reported by Ransom-ISAC/ReliaQuest and the article's confirmed SHA256 55a1eb...30c — both are extremely high fidelity as legitimate Windchill never writes randomly-named JSPs into the login servlet dir. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/cl0p-affiliates-target-internet-exposed.html • https://ransom-isac.org/blog/clop-windchill-flexplm-exploitation/ • https://www.securityweek.com/ptc-windchill-vulnerability-exploited-in-ransomware-campaign/ • https://www.ptc.com/en/about/trust-center/advisory-center/active-advisories/windchill-flexplm-rce-vulnerability
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PTC-authored patch or hotfix that legitimately deploys a JSP under the login path (validate against PTC KB / change ticket)
  • Windchill upgrade/redeploy writing many .jsp files at once (but not random 16-hex names)
  • Internal red-team or pentest re-testing the same CVE on a staging Windchill node
  • Backup/restore of the webapps directory replaying old file-create events
  • DR/imaging tools copying the Tomcat webapps tree to a new host
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","windchillinstaller.exe") and FolderPath !has "\\backup\\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the flagged .jsp, hash it and check against the campaign SHA256; grep IIS/Tomcat access logs for POST requests to that exact URI and the X-windchill-req: ?x8Fmgow header to confirm interactive use. 2) Contain: isolate the Windchill/FlexPLM host from the internet, delete/quarantine the webshell, rotate service-account and Windchill admin credentials, and confirm CVE-2026-12569 patch (June 17 2026+) is applied. 3) Hunt: sweep all Windchill nodes for other [0-9a-f]{16}.jsp / dpr_*.jsp files and flst.txt, review java/Tomcat child processes for command execution, and check egress to the four Clop C2 IPs.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FileName endswith ".jsp"
        and (FolderPath has @"\Windchill\login\" or FolderPath contains "/Windchill/login/")
        and FileName matches regex @"^(?i)([0-9a-f]{16}|dpr_[0-9a-f]{8})\.jsp$")
     or SHA256 =~ "55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (TargetFileName endswith ".jsp"
        and TargetFilePath has "Windchill" and TargetFilePath has "login"
        and TargetFileName matches regex @"^(?i)([0-9a-f]{16}|dpr_[0-9a-f]{8})\.jsp$")
     or TargetFileSHA256 =~ "55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

POST to hex-named JSP webshell under /Windchill/login/ in web/proxy logs AIExploitation Medium
Hunts web-server access logs for HTTP POST requests targeting the campaign's hex-named JSP webshells (/Windchill/login/[0-9a-f]{16}.jsp or dpr_<8hex>.jsp), the interactive-use signal for Clop's CVE-2026-12569 webshells. Optionally pivots on requests from the four known Clop exploitation IPs. Rationale: The /Windchill/login/[0-9a-f]{16}.jsp and dpr_<8hex>.jsp URI convention plus the X-windchill-req: ?x8Fmgow exploitation header were published by Ransom-ISAC/ReliaQuest; a POST to a randomly-hex-named JSP in the login servlet path is unambiguous webshell interaction. Left Defender/Falcon/Datadog/CloudWatch empty because raw web-server URI+method telemetry isn't in Defender AH DeviceNetworkEvents, FDR, or the listed Datadog/CWLI sources — this pivots on IIS/Tomcat/WAF logs. Cross-checked against: • https://ransom-isac.org/blog/clop-windchill-flexplm-exploitation/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/cl0p-affiliates-target-internet-exposed.html • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/29/ptc-windchill-cve-2026-12569-exploited/
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vulnerability scanner (Nessus/Qualys) probing the CVE-2026-12569 URI pattern — check source IP against scanner ranges
  • Internal pentest replaying the exploit against a staging Windchill node
  • Web log replay/ingestion of historical data after a SIEM re-index
  • Legitimate Windchill JSP endpoints that happen to be 16-char but non-hex (regex requires strict [0-9a-f], reducing this)
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !has "Nessus" and csUserAgent !has "Qualys" and cIP !in ("10.0.0.0/8")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm scStatus/response — a 200 to the POST means the shell executed; correlate cIP against the four Clop C2 IPs and check the User-Agent and for the X-windchill-req: ?x8Fmgow header in raw logs. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the perimeter, take the Windchill host off the internet, and quarantine the referenced JSP file on disk. 3) Hunt: enumerate all POSTs to /Windchill/login/*.jsp across the estate, pivot to file-drop and Java-child-process detections on the same host, and review outbound data volume for exfiltration.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/Windchill/login/([0-9a-f]{16}|dpr_[0-9a-f]{8})\.jsp$"
| extend KnownC2 = iff(cIP in ("216.152.148.54","216.152.151.204","104.243.35.63","5.180.41.35"), "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, scStatus, csUserAgent, KnownC2
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PTC Windchill Java/Tomcat process spawning shell or flst.txt recon AIExploitation High
Hunts the Windchill application process (java/tomcat, or IIS w3wp) spawning a command interpreter or reconnaissance binary, and specifically references to the campaign's flst.txt filesystem-enumeration artifact. This is post-webshell command execution in the Clop CVE-2026-12569 attacks. Rationale: Windchill/FlexPLM run on a Java/Tomcat servlet stack, so java/tomcat spawning a shell is anomalous, and flst.txt is the exact filesystem-enumeration filename ReliaQuest observed in this Clop campaign — combining the two makes a low-noise post-exploitation signal. Cross-checked against: • https://ransom-isac.org/blog/clop-windchill-flexplm-exploitation/ • https://www.securityweek.com/ptc-windchill-vulnerability-exploited-in-ransomware-campaign/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/cl0p-affiliates-target-internet-exposed.html
ATT&CKT1059.003 T1505.003 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windchill admin/maintenance scripts that legitimately shell out (e.g. scheduled cleanup jobs invoking cmd.exe)
  • Monitoring/APM agents embedded in Tomcat launching hostname.exe/ipconfig.exe for inventory
  • Windchill install/upgrade routines invoking net.exe or systeminfo.exe
  • Backup software running under the Tomcat service account spawning cmd.exe
  • A benign local file genuinely named flst.txt unrelated to the intrusion
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("WindchillMaintenance","purge","\\ptc\\Windchill\\bin\\") and AccountName endswith "$")
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the child ProcessCommandLine and the parent Java command line — confirm the parent is the Windchill Tomcat instance and look for recon chains (whoami/net/systeminfo) or references to flst.txt output. 2) Contain: kill the process tree, isolate the host, and quarantine any webshell JSP feeding the java process; rotate the Tomcat service account. 3) Hunt: search for the hex-named JSP file drops and POST access-log hits on the same host, review created files (flst.txt, archives) for staging, and check egress to the four Clop C2 IPs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","tomcat9.exe","tomcat10.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","hostname.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","nltest.exe")
     or ProcessCommandLine has "flst.txt"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("java.exe","javaw.exe","tomcat9.exe","tomcat10.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","hostname.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","nltest.exe")
     or TargetProcessCommandLine has "flst.txt"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PTC Windchill Java/Tomcat spawning shell or flst.txt recon
id: c4e9a138-72b5-4f6d-8e21-9a0c3d7f5b62
description: Detects the Windchill application process (java/tomcat/w3wp) spawning a command interpreter or recon binary, or referencing the Clop flst.txt enumeration artifact, after CVE-2026-12569 webshell deployment.
references:
  - https://ransom-isac.org/blog/clop-windchill-flexplm-exploitation/
  - https://www.securityweek.com/ptc-windchill-vulnerability-exploited-in-ransomware-campaign/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/18
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1083
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\java.exe'
      - '\javaw.exe'
      - '\tomcat9.exe'
      - '\tomcat10.exe'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\hostname.exe'
      - '\ipconfig.exe'
      - '\systeminfo.exe'
      - '\tasklist.exe'
      - '\nltest.exe'
  selection_flst:
    CommandLine|contains: 'flst.txt'
  condition: (selection_parent and selection_child) or selection_flst
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@ParentImage:(*\\java.exe OR *\\javaw.exe OR *\\tomcat9.exe OR *\\tomcat10.exe OR *\\w3wp.exe) AND @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\whoami.exe OR *\\net.exe OR *\\hostname.exe OR *\\ipconfig.exe OR *\\systeminfo.exe OR *\\tasklist.exe OR *\\nltest.exe)) OR @CommandLine:*flst.txt*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(java|javaw|tomcat\d*|w3wp)\.exe$/i
| (ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|whoami|net1?|hostname|ipconfig|systeminfo|tasklist|nltest)\.exe$/i OR regex("flst\.txt", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("java.exe","javaw.exe","tomcat9.exe","tomcat10.exe","w3wp.exe")) (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","hostname.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","nltest.exe") OR Processes.process="*flst.txt*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| table firstTime lastTime dest user parent_process_name process_name process count
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("java.exe","javaw.exe","tomcat9.exe","tomcat10.exe","w3wp.exe")) (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","hostname.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","nltest.exe") OR Processes.process="*flst.txt*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| table firstTime lastTime dest user parent_process_name process_name process count
Outbound connection to known Clop CVE-2026-12569 C2 / exploitation IPs AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on any host communicating with the four IP addresses tied to Clop's PTC Windchill/FlexPLM exploitation campaign. High-fidelity IOC match; especially critical if the source is an internet-facing Windchill/FlexPLM server. Rationale: The four IPs (216.152.148.54, 216.152.151.204, 104.243.35.63, 5.180.41.35) are the article's pre-extracted campaign IOCs, corroborated as Clop Windchill exploitation infrastructure by Ransom-ISAC — a direct IP match is inherently high fidelity and merits alerting. Cross-checked against: • https://ransom-isac.org/blog/clop-windchill-flexplm-exploitation/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/philips-and-ge-investigating-clop-ransomware-data-theft-claims/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/cl0p-affiliates-target-internet-exposed.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel or sandbox appliance intentionally reaching the IOC IPs for enrichment/detonation
  • Security researcher or IR team validating the indicators from a corporate egress
  • Shared hosting/CDN reuse where the IP later serves benign content (validate WHOIS/first-seen date)
  • Perimeter proxy logging the connection on behalf of many clients (attribute the true source host)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe","threatgrid.exe") and DeviceName !has "sandbox"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the internal source host and the initiating process — if it's a Windchill/FlexPLM/Tomcat/java process or an internet-facing PLM server, treat as confirmed compromise. 2) Contain: block the four IPs at the firewall/proxy, isolate the source host, and preserve netflow + host memory. 3) Hunt: on the source host look for the hex-named JSP webshells, java-spawned shells, and flst.txt; review outbound byte volume to these IPs for data exfiltration and confirm the CVE-2026-12569 patch state across all PTC assets.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("216.152.148.54","216.152.151.204","104.243.35.63","5.180.41.35")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("216.152.148.54","216.152.151.204","104.243.35.63","5.180.41.35")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-12569")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-12569")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-12569")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-12569")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc
